title: A queue from two stacks
hook: Taking from the wrong end means flipping everything. Or does it?

knows: a stack gives back the last thing added; a queue gives back the first (back-button-stack)
an occasional big copy can average out over many operations (list-doubling-copies)
doesNotKnow: that a queue can be built from two stacks cheaply
that each item is poured at most once

misconception: A queue made of two stacks must flip everything over on every removal.
objective: The learner can explain that with two stacks, an item is poured from the in-stack to the out-stack at most once in its life, so one slow removal pays for the fast ones and the average cost stays constant.

claims.text: Adding 1, 2, 3, 4 to the in-stack and then removing four times (pop the out-stack; pour the whole in-stack over only when the out-stack is empty) takes exactly 1 pour; each of the 4 items is moved once, 4 moves in total, and the items leave in the order 1 2 3 4.
claims.source: Builder's node script (2026-10-14), written from the rule in the question: pours 1, moved {1:1, 2:1, 3:1, 4:1}, left order 1,2,3,4. The first removal pours 4, 3, 2, 1 (1 ends on top); removals 2 to 4 find the out-stack non-empty. Demo.tsx runs the same rule. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 19): Own node sim of the rule: 1 pour, moved {1:1,2:1,3:1,4:1}, left 1 2 3 4; matches simulate() and the reveal.

claims.text: Each item is poured at most once in its life, so the average cost per operation stays constant (amortized O(1)).
claims.source: CLRS 3rd ed., exercise 10.1-6 (implement a queue using two stacks) and chapter 17, accounting method: charge each item 1 extra unit when added to pay for its single later move. Derivation: an item is only ever moved from in to out, and nothing moves from out back to in. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 19): Derivation: items move only in->out, so moves <= adds (own random sim of 100,000 ops confirms). CLRS 3e exercise 10.1-6 and ch. 17 accounting method (4e: ch. 16).

claims.text: A removal that finds the out-stack not empty needs no pour.
claims.source: It follows from the rule in the question: the pour happens only when the out-stack is empty. Stage text 'out not empty: no pour' on removals 2 to 4. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 19): Direct from the rule; stage note 'out not empty: no pour' on removals 2-4.

claims.text: This is the same accounting as list doubling.
claims.source: In list doubling (lesson list-doubling-copies) an occasional big copy is paid for by cheap adds in between; here an occasional pour is paid for by cheap removals. Both are the accounting method (CLRS ch. 17). | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 19): Both are the accounting method (CLRS 3e 17.2, dynamic tables 17.4); lesson list-doubling-copies exists in src/demos/cs.

recall.question: A queue is built from two stacks. You add 1000 items, then remove them all. Roughly how many times is each item moved between stacks?
options: Once for every removal before it
recall.why: The first removal pours all 1000 items into the out-stack, once each. After that every removal just pops the out-stack, so no item moves again.
